fun_highlights: The callback card system is the game's best feature: a decision made at age 7 (keeping the book) lands again at midlife (cb_books_late), and the text names the original age — 'Read, at last with ease, the book that began everything at age 7.' This is exactly the pull that makes one more life worth starting. In the transcripts, Calla (Dy.4 founder) has the book callback at 50, Beatrix passes it forward at 47, and Tobias passes it to Felix who finds it again. Each instance feels earned, not mechanical.

The drifter arc (vocation='adrift') is a genuine structural divergence. Noor Okonkwo's life (Dy.4, gen 3) and Mira Halloran (Dy.12) both go uncalled, but their adult beats are genuinely different from each other and from soldier/scholar lives: a_adrift_work, m_adrift_reckon, e_adrift_old all fire with prose specific to the uncalled shape. The three-way closing choice ('Count the roads not closed' vs 'Count the doors a fixed life would have opened') has real moral weight.

The era system visibly shapes opening texture: Hale Okonkwo (Dy.4, gen 5) is born into plague and his childhood card reads 'a sickness in the land, doors kept shut'; Calla's youth reads 'war somewhere past the edge of everything'; Beatrix's is 'lean time — a house counting every coin.' This is quick variety with low cost, and the w_plague_tend card ('breathed the same close air as the dying because they should not die alone, and was lucky, and was changed') lands with genuine weight in several lives.

The house-reputation layer creates meaningful session-to-session texture. The Okonkwo dynasty earns 'We earn the bread we eat,' the Thorne dynasty earns 'We do not save ourselves for later,' and each motto was preceded by a traceable pattern of choices. When Hale (gen 5) at age 29 chooses 'Honour the first of the line,' the card literally names Calla, five generations back — this cross-generational payoff is the genre's promise fulfilled.

Several individual lines of prose are genuinely good and carry the meditative register: 'The marriage broke on what she did. Hale left, and was right to.' (Dy.4, Calla); 'Let the road end, finally, in one place with one set of faces — and was surprised how much like relief it felt.' (a_wanderer_settle); 'Kept the question for evenings and the paid work for days, and made, between them, a sufficient life.' These are economical and exact.

The 'competing goods' cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) break the game's otherwise frequent binary of virtue vs. vice. In Dynasty 4, Noor's 'Chose the truth others had a right to over the loyalty she wanted to keep, and paid for the choosing in a friendship' is a genuinely uncomfortable choice that colours her late life. This is the game at its best: no clean answer.
staleness: The marriage beat is the loudest repeated event in the transcripts and the text pool cycles faster than the cooldown prevents. Across the 15 dynasties, every coupled adult eventually hits a_marry, and the prompt pool's seven variants ('kept rehearsing the question', 'assumed it for years', etc.) recur visibly within a single session. Dynasty 6 (Cassian Thorne) 'Married Noor young'; Dynasty 9 (Selma Quint) 'Married Cassian on an ordinary day'; Dynasty 13 (Anders Lindqvist gen 5) 'Married Ottilie on an ordinary day, and meant every word of it.' 'On an ordinary day, and meant every word of it' appears verbatim in Dynasties 1, 9, 13, and 14.

The body-decline observation pool dominates the back half of every long life. Because observe() fires up to 4 obs-events per life and vit_tire and vit_neg cover different thresholds, most lives aged 60+ string 2–3 body lines together: 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them' / 'The body has begun sending its small bills' / 'The body has begun rounding their ambitions down.' Within a single session, the phrases 'the body has begun' and 'the stairs' feel like a template — Dynasty 2 (Henrik, age 85), Dynasty 3 (Cassian, age 57), Dynasty 13 (Idris at 55, Anders at 74), Dynasty 15 (Anders at 83) all fire nearly identical body-decline ambient lines in quick succession.

The epitaph pool has only two dominant clusters across long play. 'Gave away everything they knew, and so kept it' is the teacher epitaph and appears verbatim for Selma Quint (Dy.9) and Tobias Aldecott (Dy.10 founder). 'Left more behind than they took, and the difference is what remains' appears for Mira Halloran (Dy.12) and Annika Aldecott (Dy.14, gen 2). The 'built something that outlasted the building of it' line appears for Saoirse Holloway (Dy.1) AND Tobias Aldecott (Dy.10), both founders; the game has a RECENT_CLUSTERS guard but clearly within a dense session its 14-entry window isn't enough.

The 'Look away from the outcast child / look away again' callback (c_friend + cb_lookaway) fires in nearly every life that lacks a childhood friend. Emory Lindqvist (Dy.13 gen 1) 'Looked away from a lonely child, and the small shame of it stayed' — then at 47 'Looked away a second time, and knew, now, exactly what it cost.' Mira Halloran (Dy.12) does the exact same sequence at ages 7 and 49. Dynasty 5 (Ottilie) doesn't trigger it, but a reader who plays three lives in a row is likely to see it twice. The setup/callback is good writing; the frequency drains it.

The 'public failure' choice (a_public_fall: 'Own it. Stand in the wreck' vs. 'Bury it. Move on fast.') lands in an extremely wide window (30–58, w:2, no onceDyn gate) and appears in 8 of the 15 dynasties' transcripts. The 'Own it. Stand in the wreck' outcome text is identical each time: 'Stood in the wreck of a public failure and did not look away — and people remembered that longer than the failure.' Because the outcome text never varies, the card reads as a formality by dynasty 4.

The health scare (m_health) fires with a once:true guard but its three outcome texts are short and the 'Carry on as before' result always logs 'Took the warning in, set it down, and went on exactly as before — for better and for worse.' This appears nearly verbatim in Elias Okonkwo (Dy.4 gen 2, age 45), Henrik Vane (Dy.2 elided), and Thorne gen 2 Cassian. onceDyn:4 would help but the problem is that the text is exhausted before the cooldown triggers.

improvements.what: Expand a_marry outcome-text pool for the 'on an ordinary day, and meant every word of it' line by 6–8 new variants, and add onceDyn:3 so a single session cannot see the same phrasing in consecutive lives.
improvements.why: Marriage is the most-seen beat: every life with a 'love' relation hits it and the pool has only ~8 marriage lines for the mid-age bracket. 'On an ordinary day, and meant every word of it' appears verbatim in Dynasties 1, 9, 13, 14 — visible staleness within a 2-hour session.

improvements.what: Add onceDyn:2 to the a_public_fall card and write 3 new outcome-text variants for the 'own it' path that differ structurally (not just synonyms), e.g., one that names what was staked and one that shows a relationship consequence.
improvements.why: a_public_fall has w:2, no onceDyn, a_once guard only per-life, and appears in 8/15 dynasties. The identical outcome text for 'Own it' ('stood in the wreck…and people remembered that longer than the failure') is repeated across lives without variation — a reader clocks the template by dynasty 4.

improvements.what: Reduce the observe() per-life obs cap (P._obsN) from 4 to 3, OR require that vit_tire and vit_neg cannot both fire in the same life by checking if the other already fired.
improvements.why: The transcripts show 3–4 body-decline ambient lines chaining in the back half of long lives. The phrases 'the body has begun' and 'the stairs' read as a template when seen twice in the same life and many times in a session. A per-life cap of 3 total obs, or preventing both vit pools from firing, would cut visible repetition without losing body-decline texture.

improvements.what: Gate cb_lookaway with onceDyn:4 instead of onceDyn:4-already-but-check-the-code (currently onceDyn:4 is set, which is correct); additionally add one more setup variant to c_friend's 'Look away' outcome so the first beat text doesn't match the callback's explicit reference ('the lonely child in the yard').
improvements.why: The setup ('looked away from a lonely child, and the small shame of it stayed') and the callback ('feels the decades fold: the same averted glance…') are well-written, but the callback's text quotes the setup almost exactly, which underlines the mechanical nature of the system. A varied setup line that cb_lookaway's text can't re-echo would make the callback feel earned rather than scripted.

improvements.what: Increase RECENT_CLUSTERS window from 14 to 20 entries, and add explicit blocking so 'built'/'teacher'/'kind' clusters cannot each appear more than twice in any 6-dynasty stretch.
improvements.why: In the 15-dynasty transcript, 'built something that outlasted the building of it' appears for both Dy.1 and Dy.10 founders; 'gave away everything they knew, and so kept it' is the epitaph for both Selma Quint (Dy.9) and Tobias Aldecott (Dy.10). The existing RECENT_CLUSTERS guard clears after 14 entries, which is too short for a dense reading session where dynasties average 1–2 generations.

verdict: A Life has real genre credentials: the writing is precise and often beautiful, the callback system closes arcs in a way that feels like living consequence rather than mechanical scheduling, and the era+vocation combination gives lives structurally different shapes. The first 2–3 lives of a session offer genuine pull — the opening childhood feels varied, the drifter arc is a real fourth path, and the first time a dynasty motto crystallises and is named in the very life that earned it is a genuine pay-off moment. The problem is that a session of 4+ lives starts to reveal the template: the marriage beat and the public-failure card text repeat verbatim, the body-decline ambient pool strings the same phrases in the same order, and the epitaph clusters collide faster than the guards prevent. A first session grades solidly above average — there is real content and the staleness hasn't fully landed yet — but the game is within one session's play of feeling like it has shown you most of what it has.
